card.band: 4 h. A frontier agent knows the table/polynomial approach and gets the first speedup; the accuracy gate and special cases need care. A weaker model fails the ULP bound. Buckets: one per function.
card.cheat: Lower-precision approximations are rejected by the ULP gate. Calling libm via ccall is allowed only if it is slower than the baseline, which the benchmark shows.
card.grading: Hard gate: max error under 1 ULP (pow under 1.0 ULP) and exact special-case behaviour (NaN, Inf, signed zero, subnormal) on millions of hidden points, checked against BigFloat. Score is median wall-clock over benchmark sweeps, mapped by 2^u-1 against our reference speedup S.
card.reference: The algorithms from Julia's Base.Math and its pow PR, written down in the base's API (about 500 lines). Speedup is measured on the grading machine. Julia must be shippable as an offline toolchain, which the bundle checks.
card.source: https://github.com/JuliaLang/julia/pull/42271 and the Base.Math code at v1.13.2, MIT
card.task: /app ships a Julia package with straightforward Float64 pow, exp, log, exp2, log2, and cbrt implementations, accurate but slow, wrapped as a vectorizable API. The agent rewrites them with table-driven, FMA and range-reduction methods to be faster, without losing accuracy.

spike_plan.kill_if: Base.exp or Base.^ remains callable from the package (expected), or the ccall rule cannot be enforced without source inspection.
spike_plan.pass_if: The shipped runtime can make Base.exp and Base.^ unreachable from the package, and the ccall rule has an objective, non-grep test.
steps: In a throwaway networked container, install Julia 1.13.2 and confirm the offline toolchain runs.
Write a minimal package that calls Base.exp(x) and Base.:^(x,y) and check the accuracy and timing against a naive baseline.
Check whether the reference can be hidden from the package: remove base/special from the shipped tree and see whether Base.exp still resolves from the sysimage.
Check whether a ccall to glibc libm exp/pow passes the 1 ULP gate and beats the baseline, to test the ccall rule.
Decide: if Base math cannot be made unreachable from the package, kill.

v1.summary: The seed's reference is confirmed as public: Julia v1.13.2 base/special exp.jl (256-entry table, pure Julia) and pow.jl, plus merged PR #42271, all MIT. It is killed as K11 because the same Base functions ship inside the required offline Julia runtime, so the agent can call them directly and the reference cannot be sealed.
